newsitem.title: UK: UK court overturns verdict in policeman's killing.
newsitem.headline: UK court overturns verdict in policeman's killing.

text.p: Britain's highest court on Thursday freed a teenager who had been jailed for life for murdering a policeman even though he was in handcuffs and and 100 yards (metres) away from the scene when the killing took place.

Five judges sitting in the House of Lords (upper house of parliament) overturned the 1994 conviction of Philip English and said they would give reasons for their decision at a later date. English was 15 when the policeman was stabbed to death after being called to a family row at a house in the northeastern English town of Gateshead.

A fight broke out between English, his co-defendant Paul Weddle and the policeman, but English ran away. He was arrested by police waiting round the corner, but Weddle remained in the house and fatally stabbed a police officer.

At the trial, a jury unanimously found Weddle guilty and convicted English with a 10-2 majority on the grounds that, even though he was not there when the policeman was killed, he was party to an agreement to attack the officer.
English, now 19, is believed to be the youngest person in Britain to have been found guilty of murdering a policeman.
His lawyers argued that he was wrongly convicted because of a flaw in the law and should not have been held responsible for the crime.
